title: ISRM cross-language result record
description: The single result shape every language runner (Julia, Rust, Python) emits after computing the InMAP ISRM tutorial from an isrm*.esm model. Comparing these files is what makes the three runners a cross-language agreement test rather than three independent scripts. Field-by-field tolerances live in compare_results.py, not here.

binding.description: Which language binding produced this record.

binding_version.description: Version/commit of the EarthSciAST binding used, for provenance.

model.description: Basename of the .esm driven, e.g. "isrm_point.esm". Records from different model files are comparable only if the models are numerically equivalent — isrm_point.esm and its pre-split predecessor isrm.esm are (the split into isrm_base.esm + isrm_point.esm is a pure factoring, verified by re-expansion), as were isrm_clean.esm and isrm_pushdown.esm.

mode.description: How the numbers were produced. "runtime_observed_graph": every value came from the binding's own evaluation of the .esm observed graph — the strict bar. "oracle_step0": hand-written STEP-0 arithmetic over the loader outputs, i.e. a reference oracle, NOT a demonstration that the binding executes the spec.

grid.description: Problem dimensions. Records with differing dimensions are not comparable.

n_src.description: Source cells on the SR axis (52411 at full scale).

n_rec.description: Recognized-pathway EGU FF10 emission records (43650 at full scale).

ppl.description: The emission-bearing source-cell support set — the spatial join's output. This is INTEGER-valued, so it MUST be bit-identical across bindings (CONFORMANCE_SPEC §5.5: the distinct member set is byte-identical regardless of candidate-generation backend). Any difference here is a real disagreement, never float noise.

count.description: Number of unique emission-bearing source cells (1520 at full scale).

ids.description: The full sorted 1-based source-cell id list. Optional in the file (it is `count` integers), but when present it is compared elementwise.

sha256.description: sha256 over the sorted 1-based ids serialized as decimal strings joined by "," (ASCII, no spaces, no trailing separator). Language-independent by construction.

pathways.description: Per-pathway intermediates, keyed by SR array name (SOA, pNO3, pNH4, pSO4, PrimaryPM25). Catching a disagreement here localizes it to one pathway instead of only surfacing in the death totals.

emis_sum.description: Sum of binned emissions feeding this pathway (tons/yr).

conc_sum.description: Sum over receptors of this pathway's concentration contribution, BEFORE the fact= 28766.639 scaling.

conc_max.description: Max over receptors of this pathway's concentration contribution.

plume.description: Plume rise: how each record's mass is split across the SR matrix's three emission layers, and how much mass that puts in each layer. OPTIONAL only because records predating plume rise exist (contract/records/ground-level-only/); every record from a document that states plume rise MUST carry it, and a runner that omits it is not reporting the physics it computed. Everything here comes from the document's own `sr_lower` / `stack_layer` / `w_sr0..2` observeds and its `E_<pathway>_L<layer>` binning aggregates — a runner recomputing any of it would be asserting on its own arithmetic instead of on the spec. NOTE THE SHAPE CHANGE: a record used to be charged to ONE SR layer, and this block carried a per-record `sr_layer` digest. InMAP's sr.Reader.layerFracs splits a record across TWO layers whenever its model layer falls strictly between two entries of `layers` = [0, 3, 6], so a single per-record layer no longer describes the model and `sr_layer` is gone. What replaces it: `sr_lower`, the integer index of the lower of the (at most two) layers, compared EXACTLY the way `ppl` is; `weights`, the three float shares, compared the way every other float in this record is; and `pathways`, the emitted mass per SR layer, which is what the contract really checks. `contract/records/plume_oracle.json` is the independent, SR-free reference all of it is checked against.

sr_lower.description: The document's `sr_lower` observed, one value per emission record: the LOWER of the (at most two) SR emission layers the record's mass is charged to — the index sr.Reader.layerFracs returns first. 0 for a plume at or below model layer 2, 1 for model layers 3-5, 2 for model layer 6 and above (which folds in InMAP's AboveTopErr clamp). Integer-valued, so it is compared EXACTLY; together with `weights` it reconstructs the whole assignment, because the upper layer, when there is one, is always sr_lower + 1.

count.description: Number of records hashed; equals grid.n_rec.

histogram.description: Record counts by lower SR layer 0, 1, 2.

sha256.description: sha256 over the per-record lower SR layer as ASCII decimals joined by "," in RECORD ORDER (int_seq_sha256 in results.py/.jl/contract.rs) — the same wire format as ppl_sha256 but unsorted, because a per-record field is a sequence whose order is part of the value.

weights.description: The document's `w_sr0` / `w_sr1` / `w_sr2` observeds — sr.Reader.layerFracs's per-record fractions, one field of length grid.n_rec each. These are FLOATS, unlike the layer assignment they replace, so they carry the same FieldSummary shape and the same tolerance as every other float field here: `sum`/`min`/`max`/`sample` within RTOL_FIELD, `sha256` informative rather than asserted (the fractions descend from `plume_height`, whose cube roots differ by an ulp between languages, so bit-identity across bindings is not expected). The teeth are elsewhere: `sr_lower` is exact, and `pathways.by_sr_layer` is these weights integrated against emitted mass.

max_sum_error.description: max over records of |w_sr0 + w_sr1 + w_sr2 - 1|. layerFracs conserves mass — every record's weights sum to exactly 1 — so this is float noise (~1e-16) or a broken document. Checked against an ABSOLUTE bound, not a relative one.

w_sr0.description: Share of each record's mass charged to SR emission layer 0.

w_sr1.description: Share of each record's mass charged to SR emission layer 1.

w_sr2.description: Share of each record's mass charged to SR emission layer 2.

stack_layer.description: The document's `stack_layer` observed: the model layer the STACK TOP sits in, which selects the meteorology plume rise is computed from. Separate from sr_lower because it localizes a disagreement — a wrong stack_layer means the met gather is wrong, a right stack_layer with a wrong SR assignment means the ASME expression or the layerFracs interpolation is.

histogram.description: Record counts by stack layer over ALL records, so bin 0 includes the zero-height stacks (1100 at full scale, which never enter plume rise). At least four bins: the document's in-bounds argument caps the stack layer at 3 for this inventory, and a fifth bin means that argument no longer holds. [30413, 8460, 3899, 878] at full scale.

sha256.description: int_seq_sha256 over the per-record stack layer, record order.

pathways.description: Emitted mass split across the three SR layers, per pathway, keyed by SR array name exactly as the top-level `pathways` block is. This is where the physics becomes visible as mass: at full scale SOx is 0.5/4.3/95.2% across layers 0/1/2, where a ground-level-only document puts 100% in layer 0.

by_sr_layer.description: Sum over source cells of E_<pathway>_L0, _L1, _L2 (tons/yr) — the per-record layerFracs weights integrated against emitted mass. Their total is the pathway's `emis_sum` — plume rise moves mass between layers, never into or out of a pathway, and a record split across two layers contributes a share to each.

total_pm25.description: The fact-scaled total PM2.5 concentration field over receptors.

deaths.description: Attributable-death fields. The tutorial targets are sum(krewski)=7524.918845602511 and sum(lepeule)=16979.632171487083.

timing.description: Non-comparable provenance: wall-clock, peak RSS, fetched bytes. Recorded for the writeup, never asserted on.

FieldSummary.description: Summary of one length-n_rcv float field. `sum` alone is a weak check (cancellation hides per-cell disagreement), so a fixed-index `sample` is required alongside it. `sha256` additionally pins bit-identity where that is expected — across bindings it is NOT expected, since float reduction order differs.

sample.description: Values at the 25 fixed 1-based indices defined by sample_indices() in compare_results.py: for k=0..24, idx_k = 1 + (k*(n_rcv-1) + 12) div 24, using INTEGER division throughout so the index set cannot drift between languages' float rounding modes. Evenly spans the grid.

sha256.description: sha256 over the full field as little-endian IEEE-754 float64 bytes. Equal ⇒ bit-identical fields. Unequal ⇒ INCONCLUSIVE, not a failure — compare `sum`/`sample` within tolerance instead. Note -0.0 and +0.0 compare equal as numbers but hash differently, so a field containing zeros can hash differently while being numerically identical.
